content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Reverent devotion, honor, and self-surrender directed to God. In Christian teaching, worship signifies acknowledging God’s supreme worth and sovereignty through praise, prayer, thanksgiving, service, obedience, and sacrificial dedication.","primary_basis":["Exodus 20:3-6 — exclusive devotion to God and prohibition of idolatrous worship.","Psalm 95:1-7 — praise, bowing, and kneeling before the Creator and covenant God.","Matthew 4:10; Luke 4:8 — worship and service belong to God alone.","John 4:23-24 — true worship is offered to the Father “in spirit and truth.”","Romans 12:1-2 — presenting one’s whole life to God as a living sacrifice and spiritual worship/service.","Hebrews 12:28-29 — acceptable worship is associated with reverence and awe.","Revelation 4:8-11; 5:8-14 — heavenly worship acknowledges God’s and the Lamb’s worthiness, sovereignty, and redemptive work."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Corporate liturgy or acts of praise—singing, prayer, preaching, sacraments, offerings, and other gathered-church practices.","basis":["Acts 2:42-47","1 Corinthians 11:17-34; 14:26","Ephesians 5:18-20","Colossians 3:16-17"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Whole-life obedience and service rather than primarily a religious ceremony; worship symbolizes comprehensive dedication of body, conduct, vocation, and moral life to God.","basis":["1 Samuel 15:22","Romans 12:1-2","Colossians 3:17,23-24","James 1:27"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Sacrifice or offering: biblical worship is interpreted through temple sacrifice and, in Christian theology, through Christ’s self-offering and believers’ spiritual sacrifices.","basis":["Leviticus 1-7","Hebrews 9:11-14; 10:1-14","Romans 12:1","1 Peter 2:5","Hebrews 13:15-16"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Allegiance or submission to a ruler. This is especially prominent in apocalyptic interpretation, where worship of God and the Lamb contrasts with worship of the beast and represents competing loyalties.","basis":["Daniel 3:1-18","Matthew 4:8-10","Revelation 13:4-15; 14:6-12; 19:10; 22:8-9"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Intimate communion with, encounter with, or enjoyment of God’s presence, sometimes treated as the deepest symbolic significance of worship.","basis":["Psalm 27:4","Psalm 63:1-5","John 4:23-24","2 Corinthians 3:18"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus about worship’s ordinary theological sense—honoring and devoting oneself to God—but no single settled symbolic interpretation. Scripture presents worship through overlapping images and practices, including prostration, praise, sacrifice, service, obedience, communion, and allegiance. Different Christian traditions emphasize these dimensions differently."}
